timing.description: Decision = submission of a pre-signed ladder order 200-500 ms after a tick-level MICROPRICE move of the BTC/ETH perps and spot (Binance, OKX, Bybit) toward the outcome: live lag profile peaks at [m-400, m-200) and vanishes 100 ms after the match; the hazard of a match rises 2.3% -> 8.7% with the signed tick (trigger, not correlate; necessary, low base hazard). Historically presence on block seconds 0.875 vs pure baseline 0.819.

side.description: Per decision (live): the direction of the perp microprice move over [m-600, m-100) ms (ten-series vote 86% / 83% / 75% in three live intervals, stable by vote strength: 90-97% with >= 5 agreeing series, 64-66% with one; six-series exam-feed vote 80% on 62% of decisions); per taker order at the block clock 72.7% pooled (XM 73.1%, GF 74.6%, DS 71.8%; market-only 59.9%); per one-sided block second 76.7%; buys both outcomes in 99.8% of windows pooled; buys the underdog more as |p-0.5| grows (58% small / 69% big at 0.3-0.4 vs others 35%), also at static prices.

price.description: Limit = the touch of the chosen outcome at the decision (trivial touch anchor, stated as such): VALIDATE calldata 95.1% within a tick; live 93% against the recorded ask 50 ms before the match; 16.8% of orders are priced 1+ c above the best consumed ask (100-share orders 41.7%, 30-share 11.6%; 35% late in the window): a large order is usually also a higher ladder level.

size.description: Fixed (small, large) menu per day signed at every price; large share is a per-wallet setting (DS 8%, GF 33%, XM 13%) PLUS an event-level component (both-large across wallets 1.68x independence vs null 0.75, p=0.0005) that block-clock features do not predict (within-wallet AUC 0.44-0.59). The size class carries the replicable PnL (oracle 30-share 0.41 vs size-class 0.88 pooled).

exit.description: Taker remainders (59% of orders) rest as GTC for at most a few seconds (refills <= 3 s, removal bound median 5 s) and are cancelled; holds to resolution; no sells, merges, splits or conversions; one REDEEM per window; daily TAKER_REBATE = 0.5 x prior-day taker fees (~85% of income) and MAKER_REBATE; no liquidity or holding rewards.

strategy_statement: One operator runs a TypeScript clob-client bot on four wallets [VALIDATE-only]. For every BTC 5-minute Up/Down window it pre-signs a ladder of BUY limit orders on both outcomes at every cent, in bursts 90 s before the open and at +42 s and +173 s, signing the wallets one after another [VALIDATE-only, calldata]. It submits a pre-signed order at the current touch of the outcome toward which the BTC/ETH perpetuals' microprice just ticked: live, the side information peaks 200-500 ms before the match and vanishes right after it, and the hazard of a match rises about fourfold with the size of the tick toward the outcome (a trigger, not a correlate) [VALIDATE-only: live development block]; the ten-series vote gives the side of 75-86% of taker decisions in three successive live intervals [VALIDATE-only]. The limit is the touch (95% within a tick from calldata) [VALIDATE-only]; an unfilled remainder rests for at most a few seconds and is cancelled [VALIDATE-only]. Sizes come from a fixed daily menu (30/60/100); the large size is partly chosen per event across wallets, but nothing measured at the block clock predicts it [VALIDATE-only]. It buys both outcomes in almost every window, tilts toward the underdog as prices leave 0.5, and holds to resolution [VALIDATE-only]. About 85% of its income is the 50% taker-fee rebate on its volume; trading after fees is near break-even [VALIDATE-only]. Per-window PnL is a sum of order-level bets (split-half ~0), so replicating it requires the same orders and sizes: with a fixed 30-share size and >= 2 s latency even the wallet's own decisions reach only 0.14-0.40 [VALIDATE-only]. Nothing is exam-verified.
